screens.name: Home — empty omen and populated omen
screens.evidence: Sheets 12–13 show both omen states and the entrance pair; supplied runtime evidence reports enlarged-layout, navigation-clearance and reduced-motion checks.
findings: Give the rotating example question a steadier visible presence so it contributes to discovery throughout the entrance.

screens.name: Approach — opening
screens.evidence: Sheet 02 shows a consistent opening composition across the paired captures, and runtime evidence reports immediate approach under reduced motion.
findings: Retain the explicit next-step explanation and verify the opening status is announced once to assistive technology.

screens.name: Question composer — self
screens.evidence: Sheets 02 and 04 show normal and enlarged composition with a prominent input, while supplied evidence reports four-line capacity and keyboard checks.
findings: Replace “your prediction engine” with a concrete explanation of where submitted questions and answers go.

screens.name: Question composer — named person retained
screens.evidence: Sheets 03 and 20–21 show Alex retained at both sizes, and supplied runtime evidence reports draft cancellation, focus return and an actual named-person request.
findings: Make the unfocused question field's editable role clearer without relying on its distant bottom rule.

screens.name: Named-person editor — Someone selected
screens.evidence: Sheets 02–04 show the selected mode, persistent first-name label and explicit save action; supplied evidence reports validation and preserved drafts.
findings: Verify the mode choices expose a single selected state and the name field's relationship to that mode in the accessibility tree.

screens.name: Adaptive card 1 — plan readiness
screens.evidence: Sheets 04–05 show the settled and entrance states with progress, and supplied evidence reports single keyboard advancement and retained answers on Back.
findings: Make immediate advancement on choosing an answer apparent before the first selection.

screens.name: Adaptive card 2 — obstacles
screens.evidence: Sheet 05 shows stable option spacing and a changed progress indicator across paired captures; supplied evidence describes retained-answer navigation.
findings: Show the retained answer unmistakably when users return to this step.

screens.name: Adaptive card 3 — support
screens.evidence: Sheets 05–06 show the final synthetic layout card and transition with four readable choices.
findings: Clarify that the final choice starts forecast preparation rather than opening another question.

screens.name: Adaptive card — custom answer, empty
screens.evidence: Sheet 06 shows normal and enlarged empty input with disabled Continue, and supplied evidence reports short-viewport preservation of the editor and Choices control.
findings: Label the escape route “Back to choices” so its purpose is explicit.

screens.name: Voice entry — unavailable and fallback
screens.evidence: Sheet 13 shows a prominent typing fallback and microphone failure notice, with actual fallback verification reported in the supplied runtime evidence.
findings: Place the microphone failure explanation closer to the retry action to reduce the distance between cause and recovery.

screens.name: Planning — loading
screens.evidence: Sheet 19 shows entrance and settled loading states with time expectation and cancellation, while supplied evidence reports real timeout and cancellation recovery.
findings: Verify a screen reader announces the planning phase without repeatedly announcing decorative animation updates.

screens.name: Research — loading
screens.evidence: Sheets 22–23 show a consistent loading composition with a research-specific explanation, and runtime evidence reports reduced-motion and timing checks.
findings: Make the change from question planning to research perceptible through the status announcement as well as the supporting text.

screens.name: Planning failure
screens.evidence: Sheets 07–08 show retry and question editing with a no-charge explanation; supplied evidence reports injected failure followed by successful retry.
findings: Verify focus reaches the error explanation before its recovery actions.

screens.name: Prediction failure
screens.evidence: Sheet 08 shows retry, review answers and edit question in a clear order, and supplied evidence reports preservation of answers and credits.
findings: Keep retry as the primary action while preserving both contextual editing routes.

screens.name: Sensitive question — planning redirect
screens.evidence: Sheets 24–25 show a support destination and explicit no-reading-spent feedback, with the redirect reported as exercised in the supplied runtime evidence.
findings: Put the brief explanation before the support button so users understand the change of task before acting.

screens.name: Sensitive question — prediction redirect
screens.evidence: Sheet 25 shows consistent settled and entrance states with support, alternative question and edit actions.
findings: Explain the redirect before presenting its primary destination and retain the explicit credit-preservation message.

screens.name: Forecast reveal
screens.evidence: Sheets 23–24 show the forecast, qualification, date and action hierarchy, while supplied evidence reports a real dated forecast and brief/deeper reasoning flow.
findings: Label the date's role explicitly so users can distinguish a forecast deadline from a check-in reminder.

screens.name: Forecast check-in — unanswered
screens.evidence: Sheet 07 shows three outcome choices above the share action, and supplied evidence reports persisted outcomes.
findings: Give the check-in task slightly more emphasis than sharing when the user opens a due forecast.

screens.name: Forecast check-in — Not quite saved
screens.evidence: Sheet 17 shows a checked answer, persistent saved label and confirmation notice, with persistence reported in the supplied evidence.
findings: Reduce redundant confirmation by letting the persistent saved state carry the outcome after a brief notice.

screens.name: Forecast check-in — Not yet saved
screens.evidence: Sheet 18 shows selected Not yet, a saved status and a contextual waiting notice.
findings: Clarify whether “Not yet” changes the next check-in date or only records the current outcome.

screens.name: Forecast check-in — Yes saved
screens.evidence: Sheet 18 shows a checked Yes, persistent Came true status and a saved confirmation.
findings: Preserve the persistent outcome while keeping the temporary confirmation from obscuring subsequent actions.

screens.name: Evidence overview — Plus
screens.evidence: Sheets 21 and 23 show four clearly described categories and enlarged reflow, while supplied evidence reports complete category access and keyboard return behavior.

screens.name: Evidence reader — Your answers
screens.evidence: Sheets 08–09 and 19–20 show long answers and enlarged focus states, with full-content and return-focus checks reported in the supplied evidence.

screens.name: Evidence reader — Assumptions
screens.evidence: Sheets 09 and 20 show normal and enlarged assumption text with explicit return navigation, and supplied evidence reports lossless reader content.
findings: Keep return navigation adjacent to the reading task and subordinate the cluster of sharing and re-asking actions.

screens.name: Evidence reader — Why this forecast
screens.evidence: Sheets 09–10 and 21–22 show separated full passages and enlarged reader focus, with normalized full-text equality reported in the supplied evidence.

screens.name: Evidence reader — Current sources
screens.evidence: Sheets 10 and 22 show long synthetic source entries with dates and publishers, while supplied evidence reports text contrast and full-category access.
findings: Separate source title, publisher and supporting description so long entries do not read as one continuous gold link.

screens.name: Free reasoning — Why this forecast
screens.evidence: Sheet 24 shows complete separated reasoning followed by an upgrade action, while supplied evidence reports maintained free/Plus boundaries.

screens.name: Share — collapsed options

screens.name: Share — expanded invite and reminder options

screens.name: Share — export preparing

screens.name: Share — export failure and retry

screens.name: Shared image inspection and story

screens.name: History — empty

limitations: This is a provisional browser assessment based on the supplied screenshots and runtime narrative; no tools, source, prior grader reports or other task state were inspected.
Dimension scores use the full provisional browser range; missing physical-device proof is recorded separately rather than imposing a blanket score reduction.
For each item, A is the mean of its applicable hierarchy, typography and surfaces scores; F is the mean of its applicable clarity, feedback and accessibility scores; overall is round(0.4A + 0.6F, 1).
The required schema has no aggregate-score fields; six dimension scores are supplied for every item, and null is reserved for genuinely inapplicable decorative dimensions.

The A>=9 and F>=9 threshold is not met across all screens and components; the age-restriction and focused birthday-editor states are stronger than the broader reading, discovery and secondary-navigation system.

No blocked primary task, data loss, error disguised as success or ignored motion preference is established by the supplied evidence; below-viewport content is not treated as unreachable given the reported scrolling and layout checks.
Paired transition captures support composition continuity but cannot independently prove animation timing, absence of transient shifts, pressed feedback or every intermediate frame.
Runtime checks are reported evidence rather than independently replayed observations; older retained checks do not establish that every unchanged boundary was rerun this round.
Fixture text and synthetic three-card flows establish layout stress coverage only, not production wording, actual adaptive counts, semantic quality or predictive accuracy.
The correction placeholder visibly loses its final character at 200%; its persistent format label prevents this observation from establishing an essential-content hard-gate failure.

Physical iPhone Safari, native Dynamic Type, VoiceOver, microphone permissions, keyboard behavior, haptics, hardware timing, real payments and OS sharing remain unverified and prevent full native certification.
Offline Circles and sample Sky captures do not establish production social or authentication behavior; a browser PNG download does not establish native delivery.
Raster qualification readability, complete star-target geometry and representative assistive-technology task completion remain unresolved despite reported DOM contrast and axe checks.
topFixes: Move date examples outside single-line inputs and make invalid-date feedback explain impossible dates.
Clean up fixed-header scroll boundaries that leave section titles visibly sliced.
Give long evidence passages semantic section labels, structured source entries and consistent return-to-forecast navigation.
Clarify disabled birth-details and Circles controls with their specific prerequisites.
Replace technical submission wording and ambiguous secondary labels with concrete user-facing descriptions.
Prove star navigation, pressed states, selected-answer return states and status announcements before claiming browser-wide A>=9 and F>=9.
